claimText: The Canaccord Genuity consent order, issued in March 2026, found at least 160 SARs unfiled and thousands of suspicious transactions flowing undetected

source.title: In the Matter of Canaccord Genuity LLC

claimText: The FCA's Financial Crime Guide (FCG 3.2.5A, last updated 29 November 2024) recognises that rule-driven monitoring can be poorly calibrated for complex or high-volume payment flows, and names machine learning and AI-based tools as examples of "sophisticated technologies" that can help firms detect suspicious activity or triage existing alerts

source.title: Financial Crime Guide, FCG 3.2.5A (The use of transaction monitoring)

claimText: FinCEN's original AML/CFT programme-effectiveness proposal, issued 3 July 2024, cited machine learning as a tool that can improve customer risk assessment and reduce false positives. That proposal was withdrawn and fully superseded by a new NPRM FinCEN issued on 7 April 2026

source.title: Fact Sheet: Proposed Rule to Fundamentally Reform Financial Institution AML/CFT Programs

claimText: The FCA can commission a skilled persons report under Section 166 of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 to independently assess a firm's transaction monitoring effectiveness

source.title: Enforcement Guide EG 3.3 (Reports by skilled persons (section 166)) / Supervision Manual SUP 5

The FCA's 8 April 2026 multi-firm review of CDD/EDD and ongoing monitoring controls found firms lacked sufficient detail on how often periodic reviews should take place and what firms were expected to do in the case of event-driven reviews, treating the two as separate controls

source.title: Firms' customer due diligence processes and controls: our findings

claimText: The FCA fined Nationwide Building Society £44,078,500 in December 2025 for anti-financial crime systems and controls failings running from October 2016 to July 2021

source.title: FCA fines Nationwide £44m for failings in financial crime controls

claimText: For most of the relevant period, in breach of its own policies, Nationwide had no process for undertaking either periodic or event-driven reviews of a large number of its customer relationships

source.title: Final Notice: Nationwide Building Society

claimText: A Nationwide customer used personal current accounts to receive 24 fraudulent Covid furlough payments totalling £27.3 million over 13 months, with £26.01 million of that deposited over 8 days

source.title: FCA fines Nationwide £44m for failings in financial crime controls

claimText: Since 2021, the FCA has imposed 13 fines totalling £300,767,526 on banks for anti-money laundering systems and controls failings

source.title: FCA fines Nationwide £44m for failings in financial crime controls

claimText: The former CFP Management Ltd MLRO was fined £465,415, the figure the Upper Tribunal endorsed in June 2025 after revising down the FCA's original £632,594 proposal

source.title: Upper Tribunal ruling in the cases of Toni Fox and David Brian Price

claimText: Under section 333A of POCA 2002, the regulated-sector tipping off offence is strict liability, no criminal intent is required, the test is only whether the disclosure is likely to prejudice an investigation

source.title: Proceeds of Crime Act 2002, section 333A

claimText: On conviction on indictment, a section 333A POCA 2002 tipping off offence carries a maximum of two years' imprisonment

source.title: Proceeds of Crime Act 2002, section 333A(4)(b)

claimText: In a 2026 industry survey of over 500 fraud, risk, and AML professionals, Incognia found 81% of institutions reporting more mule account handovers and only 16% catching the handover before any suspicious transaction moves

source.title: The State of Mule Account Handovers in 2026 Report

claimText: Under Article 5a of Regulation (EU) No 260/2012, as inserted by Regulation (EU) 2024/886, an in-scope euro transfer must settle within 10 seconds, 24 hours a day, subject to narrow carve-outs for non-euro-area providers and planned maintenance, not a blanket no-exceptions rule

source.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/886 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 March 2024, Article 5a
source.publisher: EUR-Lex (Official Journal of the European Union)

claimText: Leicestershire Police's Operation Kilo traced more than £53 million through a mule account network moved into cryptocurrency and out through Post Office branches in Leicester between 2019 and 2021, ending in five convictions carrying a combined sentence of over 35 years, the heaviest for Jigar Gheewala at 11 years and 10 months plus a 14-year company director ban

source.title: Detectives Uncover Major Money Laundering Operation

claimText: Thailand's Department of Business Development, working with the Central Investigation Bureau, has been cracking down on corporate mule bank accounts and nominee arrangements; a 2025 enforcement sweep across 46 locations implicated 442 juristic persons

source.title: Thailand Enhances the Foreign Business License (FBL) Regime and Increases Enforcement Measures against Nominee Practices and Mule Bank Account Activities
source.publisher: LawPlus Ltd., reporting on Department of Business Development / Central Investigation Bureau enforcement action

claimText: Since October 2024, most UK victims of authorised push payment fraud have a legal right to reimbursement from their bank, subject to an £85,000 cap per claim under the Payment Systems Regulator's rules; that cap remained unchanged in the PSR's July 2026 first-year evaluation, though a separate consultation on recalibrating the cap is due in December 2026

source.title: Independent Evaluation of the APP Scams Reimbursement Requirement, First Year

claimText: ACAMS's CAMS certification package costs US$1,595 (Public Sector) to US$2,095 (Private Sector) self-study, or US$2,095 to US$2,495 bundled with the Virtual Classroom Series. Active ACAMS membership is mandatory to obtain and maintain the certification. Exam retake is US$299, exam extension US$100

source.title: CAMS Certifications: How to Get CAMS Certified

claimText: CAMS requires 40 eligibility credits earned through a combination of education, professional AFC-related experience, existing certifications, and training; no higher-education degree is mandatory. ACAMS states the certification is for AFC professionals with 18 to 24 months of experience, aspiring to or working in the second or third line of defense; common roles listed include MLRO/BSA Officer, Compliance Officer, Risk Manager, Internal Auditor, Head of Compliance, Head of KYC, Head of TM

source.title: CAMS Certifications: How to Get CAMS Certified

claimText: CAMS is ACAMS's Specialist-level credential; ACAMS's own accelerated-eligibility rules state that CAMS qualifies a holder for all other Specialist and Advanced certifications without earning additional eligibility credits

source.title: CAMS Certifications: How to Get CAMS Certified

claimText: CAMS recertification is required every 3 years, with 60 total credits (at least 12 from ACAMS). All 3-year ACAMS recertifications share the same fee schedule: US$200 early (by October 1), US$250 standard (by December 15), US$300 late (by March 31)

source.title: ACAMS Recertification

claimText: ACAMS's CGSS certification package costs US$1,495 (Public Sector) to US$1,995 (Private Sector) self-study, or US$1,995 to US$2,395 bundled with the Virtual Classroom Series. Active ACAMS membership is mandatory. Exam retake is US$299, exam extension US$100

source.title: Certified Global Sanctions Specialist (CGSS) Certification

claimText: CGSS requires 40 eligibility credits, the same credit system used for CAMS. ACAMS states CGSS is for mid- to senior-level professionals responsible for sanctions compliance, screening, or managing economic and trade sanctions programmes, plus AFC, AML/CTF, legal and regulatory specialists who oversee compliance, risk management or advisory functions

source.title: Certified Global Sanctions Specialist (CGSS) Certification

claimText: CGSS is a Specialist-level ACAMS credential alongside CAMS; ACAMS's accelerated-eligibility rules let CAMS holders qualify for CGSS, and vice versa, without earning additional eligibility credits

source.title: Certified Global Sanctions Specialist (CGSS) Certification

claimText: CGSS recertification is required every 3 years, with 30 total credits (at least 15 from ACAMS), on the same US$200/US$250/US$300 fee schedule as other 3-year ACAMS recertifications

source.title: ACAMS Recertification

claimText: ACAMS's CKYCA certification package costs US$1,045, the same price for both Private and Public Sector. Active ACAMS membership is mandatory. Exam retake is US$199, exam extension US$100

source.title: CKYCA Certification

claimText: CKYCA eligibility uses ACAMS's general credit system (education, professional experience, certifications, training), with requirements set at ACAMS's Associate level, its lowest certification tier

source.title: CKYCA Certification

claimText: CKYCA is ACAMS's Associate-level certification, the tier below Specialist-level CAMS and CGSS, per ACAMS's own three-tier structure (Associate, Specialist, Advanced)

source.title: ACAMS Recertification

claimText: CKYCA (an Associate-level certification, alongside CTMA and CAFCA) requires recertification every year: 2 ACAMS credits per year, no application and no fee, automatic once requirements are met while ACAMS membership stays active

source.title: ACAMS Recertification

claimText: ACFCS's own certification-overview and dedicated certification-pricing pages render CFCS package pricing client-side; no dollar figure is present in the static page source of either. Search-engine caches of the same domain report US$1,195 (current members), US$1,395 (exam plus 1-year membership), or US$1,725 (exam plus 3-year membership), with reduced government rates from US$750, but these figures were not independently confirmed by a direct fetch

source.title: Certification Overview / Certification Pricing (search-cache reference, pricing not present in static page source)

claimText: CFCS requires active ACFCS membership plus 40 earned eligibility credits (drawn from education, professional financial-crime experience, certifications, and training; 10 credits per full year of directly relevant professional experience)

source.title: CFCS Certification Process & Eligibility

claimText: ACFCS's certification-overview page publishes no formal tier structure or ladder above CFCS, unlike ACAMS's explicit Associate/Specialist/Advanced tiering

source.title: Certification Overview

claimText: CFCS recertification is required every 3 years: 60 continuing education credits (earned through training, education, and relevant professional experience), with active ACFCS membership required throughout the cycle. ACFCS runs random recertification audits requiring supporting documentation

source.title: Recertification

claimText: The CFE Exam application fee is US$480, covering application processing and the first attempt at each required section. Exam retakes are US$110 per failed section; a two-year application-window extension costs US$150. ACFE Associate Membership is mandatory; membership dues vary by a dues calculator rather than a single flat published rate

source.title: CFE Credential FAQs

claimText: CFE eligibility requires ACFE Associate Membership, a minimum of 40 points in ACFE's eligibility points system to sit the exam, and a minimum of 50 points plus (normally) two years of fraud-related professional experience to be awarded the credential. Points come from education (a bachelor's degree yields 40 points) and/or fraud-related work experience (2 years of experience can substitute for each year of missing education)

source.title: CFE Credential Eligibility

claimText: ACFE's site publishes CFE as its single general credential with no formal higher certification tier; ACFE positions ongoing career progression through its own mentoring, job board, and career-resource programmes rather than a next-level exam

source.title: Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE) Credential

claimText: To maintain the CFE credential, holders must complete a minimum of 20 CPE credits during each annual compliance period, with at least 10 credits fraud-related and at least 2 credits ethics-related

source.title: Continuing Professional Education (CPE) Requirements

claimText: The ICA Certificate in Anti Money Laundering costs GBP765 / EUR860 / USD1,030 in course fees, plus a GBP195 / EUR220 / USD260 twelve-month ICA membership fee added at checkout for non-members

source.title: ICA Certificate in Anti Money Laundering

claimText: The ICA Certificate in AML is a Level 2, Introductory qualification with no stated formal prerequisite, positioned as suitable for anyone wanting to learn more about AML, including operational or front-line staff considering a career move into AML. It carries 20 ICA CPD hours and a 2-month duration, assessed by a one-hour online multiple-choice exam

source.title: ICA Certificate in Anti Money Laundering

claimText: The ICA Certificate in AML is ICA's Level 2 entry qualification; ICA's own qualification framework and course pages present the Level 6 Diploma in AML as the next step up

source.title: ICA Diploma in Anti Money Laundering (AML)

claimText: ICA qualifications, including the Certificate in AML, do not require recertification or retesting to remain held. ICA recommends, but does not require, 35 hours of CPD per membership year; that recommendation is tied to earning an optional Certified Practitioner Certificate badge, not to retaining the underlying qualification. Replacement certificates for ICA qualifications remain obtainable on request (a fee applies)

source.title: ICA FAQs (Membership & CPD, Course selection)

claimText: The ICA Diploma in Anti Money Laundering costs GBP4,500 / EUR5,085 / USD6,075 in course fees, plus a GBP195 / EUR220 / USD260 twelve-month ICA membership fee for non-members

source.title: ICA Diploma in Anti Money Laundering (AML)

claimText: The ICA Diploma in AML is a Level 6, Advanced qualification requiring a good standard of spoken and written English plus a sound educational background (degree or professional qualification) or equivalent. ICA states the course is suitable for MLROs/MLPOs and their deputies, police and FIU/FCU staff, managers with internal AML control responsibilities, risk managers, accountants and lawyers. It carries 130 ICA CPD hours over a 9-month, part-time format with four intakes a year

source.title: ICA Diploma in Anti Money Laundering (AML)

claimText: The ICA Diploma in AML is ICA's Level 6 Advanced tier, alongside the Diploma in Governance, Risk and Compliance; ICA's qualification framework positions its Postgraduate Diploma level above both

source.title: ICA FAQs (Course selection: ICA Qualification Framework)

claimText: Same structure as the ICA Certificate in AML: no recertification or retesting on the qualification itself; 35 CPD hours/year is recommended, not required, and tied to an optional Certified Practitioner Certificate rather than to retaining the Diploma

source.title: ICA FAQs (Membership & CPD)

claimText: The ICA Diploma in Governance, Risk and Compliance costs GBP4,500 / EUR5,085 / USD6,075 in course fees, plus a GBP195 / EUR220 / USD260 twelve-month ICA membership fee for non-members

source.title: ICA Diploma in Governance, Risk and Compliance

claimText: The ICA Diploma in GRC is a Level 6, Advanced qualification with the same English-language and educational-background entry bar as the Diploma in AML. ICA states the course is suitable for compliance officers/managers and their deputies, managers with internal compliance-control responsibilities, risk managers, internal audit staff, regulatory representatives, accountants, lawyers and company secretaries. It carries 130 ICA CPD hours over a 9-month, part-time format

source.title: ICA Diploma in Governance, Risk and Compliance

claimText: The ICA Diploma in GRC is ICA's Level 6 Advanced tier, the governance, risk and compliance counterpart to the Diploma in AML, both sitting below ICA's Postgraduate Diploma level

source.title: ICA Diploma in Governance, Risk and Compliance

claimText: Same structure as the other two ICA qualifications in this guide: no recertification or retesting on the qualification itself; 35 CPD hours/year is recommended, not required

source.title: ICA FAQs (Membership & CPD)

claimText: CCEP-I's initial exam fee is US$350 for CCB/SCCE/HCCA members and US$450 for non-members; a re-exam within the exam eligibility period costs US$75. SCCE/HCCA membership dues are separate and are not covered by the exam fee

source.title: Compliance Certification FAQs (CCB)
source.publisher: Society of Corporate Compliance and Ethics (SCCE) / Compliance Certification Board (CCB)

claimText: CCEP-I eligibility requires at least one year in a full-time compliance position, or 1,500 hours of direct compliance job duties, earned in the two years preceding the application, with duties tied to the exam's Detailed Content Outline; an alternative pathway exists via a CCB-accredited university compliance and ethics programme

source.title: Compliance Certification FAQs (CCB)
source.publisher: Society of Corporate Compliance and Ethics (SCCE) / Compliance Certification Board (CCB)

claimText: SCCE's own FAQ draws the distinction directly: CCEP certification is geared toward US compliance and ethics law and is primarily for individuals who work within the US, while CCEP-I focuses on international compliance and ethics law and is primarily for individuals who work outside the US or have international affiliates; both sit at the same CCB certification tier with no formal ladder above either

source.title: Compliance Certification FAQs (CCB)
source.publisher: Society of Corporate Compliance and Ethics (SCCE) / Compliance Certification Board (CCB)

claimText: CCB certification renewal (covering CCEP-I) is required every 2 years: 40 CCB CEUs must be earned and submitted, with a minimum of 20 CEUs from live training or events. The dollar renewal fee itself is not published on CCB's static renewal page, which points to a separate fee schedule

source.title: Renew Certification (CCB)
source.publisher: Society of Corporate Compliance and Ethics (SCCE) / Compliance Certification Board (CCB)

claimText: CISI's Level 3 Certificate in Combating Financial Crime costs a total exam fee of GBP402 plus a mandatory workbook fee of GBP210; the lighter Award tier of the same subject costs GBP155 exam fee plus GBP105 workbook fee

source.title: CISI Price List (Qualifying Level 3 Qualifications)

claimText: CISI's Combating Financial Crime qualification page states no rigid formal prerequisite; it is positioned by subject-matter fit rather than a stated minimum of years of experience or a required prior qualification

source.title: Combating Financial Crime

claimText: CISI positions Combating Financial Crime at both an Award level and a higher Certificate level; CISI's own qualification listing places its Diploma-level investment-compliance qualifications above the Certificate tier

source.title: Combating Financial Crime

claimText: CISI's Combating Financial Crime qualification does not itself require recertification or retesting. The Award tier of this qualification is stated on CISI's own page to grant Affiliate-level CISI membership only; whether that Affiliate-grant statement extends identically to the Certificate tier compared in this guide was not directly confirmed. A directly fetched CISI CPD-requirements document describes a 35-hour annual CPD scheme, which appears to apply to Chartered-level members, not Affiliate members; the CPD figure that specifically applies to Affiliate-grade members was not resolved with confidence and should be confirmed directly with CISI

source.title: Combating Financial Crime; CISI CPD Requirements document

claimText: ACAMS's Certified AFC Auditor package (formerly Advanced CAMS-Audit) costs US$1,695 (Public Sector) to US$2,195 (Private Sector) self-study, or US$2,195 to US$2,595 bundled with the Virtual Classroom Series. Active ACAMS membership is mandatory. Exam retake is US$299, exam extension US$100

source.title: ACAMS Certified AFC Auditor Certification (formerly Advanced CAMS-Audit)

claimText: Certified AFC Auditor requires either 60 ACAMS eligibility credits or an active CAMS designation. ACAMS recommends a minimum of five years of relevant experience before applying at the Advanced level, and states it is highly recommended, though not strictly mandatory, that candidates hold CAMS or equivalent knowledge of AML fundamentals

source.title: ACAMS Certified AFC Auditor Certification (formerly Advanced CAMS-Audit)

claimText: ACAMS's own product page states the certification (formerly Advanced CAMS-Audit) is for mid- to senior-level professionals conducting AFC audits or testing and monitoring AFC controls, internal audit staff, external auditors providing AFC assurance, and professionals preparing institutions for regulatory examinations; ACAMS's Advanced tier also includes CAMS-FCI (Financial Crimes Investigations) and CAMS-RM (Risk Management) as parallel senior credentials

source.title: ACAMS Certified AFC Auditor Certification (formerly Advanced CAMS-Audit)

claimText: ACAMS's dedicated recertification page lists Advanced-level certifications (Certified AFC Auditor, CAMS-FCI, CAMS-RM) at 45 total credits per 3-year cycle (at least 15 from ACAMS), on the same US$200/US$250/US$300 fee schedule as other 3-year ACAMS recertifications. Note: the Certified AFC Auditor product page's own recertification summary text still states a 30-credit figure inherited from its pre-rebrand copy; this ledger entry follows the dedicated, per-tier recertification page as the more authoritative and current source

source.title: ACAMS Recertification
